final.answer: For the valve family documented for FV-12-1, the available flow characteristics depend on the cage/trim selected: standard cages offer quick-opening, linear or equal percentage; Whisper Trim, WhisperFlo and Cavitrol cages are linear only. For the ET and EAT variants (with WCC/LCC/CF8M bonnet, sizes 1-4 full and reduced ports) the characteristic options are equal percent or linear. So all three — equal percentage, linear, and quick opening — are available, subject to the cage/trim choice.

final.answer: For a 3051CFC compact orifice meter with conditioning option C at a beta ratio of 0.50 in Range 2, you can expect a flow accuracy of ±1.95% of flow rate, which holds over an 8:1 flow turndown (i.e., from full scale down to one-eighth of full scale). For comparison, the same meter with a beta ratio of 0.4 offers ±1.75% of flow rate. Note that the datasheet also lists a general figure of "up to 1.75 percent of flow rate" for the 3051CFC, but the value specific to your configuration (β = 0.50, Option C, Range 2) is the ±1.95% figure from the flow reference accuracy table.

final.answer: The transmitter feeding FIC-10-1 is FT-10-1, a Rosemount 3051 flow transmitter. On a detected sensor or microprocessor failure, its HART 4-20 mA analog output is driven either high or low to alert the user; which direction occurs depends on whether the transmitter is configured for standard (high alarm ≥21.75 mA, low alarm ≤3.75 mA), NAMUR-compliant (≥22.5 mA / ≤3.6 mA), or custom levels (20.2–23.0 mA / 3.6–3.8 mA). The high or low failure mode is user-selectable with a jumper/switch on the transmitter.

final.answer: The valve operated by control loop FIC-11-1 is FV-11-1, a globe control valve. According to its datasheet, the valve plug seal ring is available in several soft materials with different temperature ranges: for the 2-piece seal (standard for NPS 1-6 valves except those with Cavitrol III cages), carbon-filled PTFE is rated -73 to 232 °C (-100 to 450 °F), ethylene-propylene -40 to 232 °C (-40 to 450 °F), fluorocarbon -18 to 204 °C (0 to 400 °F), and nitrile -40 to 71 °C (-40 to 160 °F) for air and hydrocarbons or -40 to 82 °C (-40 to 180 °F) for other compatible fluids. For the spring-loaded seal (standard for the NPS 8 valve and for NPS 1-6 valves with Cavitrol III cages), PTFE with an N10276 spring is rated -73 to 232 °C (-100 to 450 °F), and PTFE/graphite with an R30003 spring (used with PEEK anti-extrusion rings) is rated -73 to 316 °C (-100 to 600 °F) in non-oxidizing service but limited to 260 °C (500 °F) in oxidizing service. The PEEK anti-extrusion rings themselves are not temperature-limiting. Above 232 °C (450 °F), PEEK anti-extrusion rings with spring-loaded seal rings are required to reach the higher limits. No separate piston ring part is named in the datasheet; the seal-related parts it lists are the seal ring, backup ring, retaining ring and PEEK anti-extrusion rings.

final.answer: The datasheet for FV-16-2 (Fisher ET/EAT/ETR, fisher-et-d100022x012) does not give a single Cv at full open for a 2 inch valve, and it also does not state which valve type FV-16-2 actually is. What it does give are maximum flow coefficients (Cv) at maximum valve plug travel — i.e. fully open, full-sized trim, equal percentage cage, normal flow direction — per valve type and size, from Table 17 on page 23: for a 2 inch valve, EAT with liner 48.1, EAT without liner 47.2, ED 59.7, and ETR 59.7. Since the available facts do not tie FV-16-2 to one of these types, the specific Cv at full open for this valve cannot be determined; it is 48.1 (EAT with liner), 47.2 (EAT without liner), or 59.7 (ED or ETR) depending on the type.

final.answer: FV-11-1 can be supplied with flanged ends — this is not limited to buttweld or screwed connections. The available-constructions data shows raised-face or ring-type-joint flanged end connections in class ratings CL150, CL300 and CL600 (flat-faced CL125 and raised-face CL250 for cast iron bodies), as well as flanged connections per EN 1092-1/B at pressure ratings PN16 through PN100. Buttweld, screwed and socket-weld ends are also available options, so flanged ends are offered alongside those alternatives.

final.answer: GV-12-3 is described as a Type 165 2/2-way solenoid valve, so yes, it needs electrical power to operate. The datasheet lists supply voltages of 24V DC, 230V 50/60Hz and 115V 50/60Hz, so 24 V DC will work and you do not need 230 V AC. Variants are available with EPDM or FKM gaskets for each of the 24V DC, 110V AC and 230V AC coil voltages; use the voltage and current type given on the valve's type plate, with a tolerance of ±10%. Power consumption is low: on AC, 20 VA at inrush and 11 VA in operation (5 W on DC); the electrical connection is a cable plug (appliance plug, IP65).

final.answer: FV-10-1 is described by a Fisher ET/EAT/ETR control valve bulletin. The available body materials are cast iron, WCC carbon steel or LCC carbon steel, WC9 chrome moly steel, CF8M (cast 316 stainless steel), and CF3M (cast 316L stainless steel), with other materials available upon request. Yes, stainless steel bodies are available — CF8M (316 SS) and CF3M (316L SS) — which suits corrosive service, and optional sour service (NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 and MR0103) materials are also offered; hardened stainless steel trim is standard and the valves are offered in steel/stainless screwed, welded or flanged constructions.

final.answer: The item directly upstream of BV-1-2 is pump P-1-4. According to its datasheet (Gorman-Rupp 0700286, Pump Specifications, p. 1), the casing is made of ductile iron and the impeller is made of Gray Iron 40 (an enclosed, six-vane impeller). The datasheet does not say whether the pump is suitable for slightly acidic water around pH 5 — no pH range or chemical-compatibility information is specified anywhere in it. It only lists materials of construction (ductile iron casing and seal plate, gray iron 40 impeller, gray iron 25 wear rings and bearing housing, steel 1045 shaft, nitrile gaskets, silicon carbide seal faces, Viton elastomers, stainless 316 shaft sleeve and spring) and states the pumped medium as water or petroleum in the performance curves, so suitability for acidic water would need to be confirmed with the manufacturer.

final.answer: The valve in loop FIC-10-1 is FV-10-1, documented as a Fisher easy-e ET/EAT/ETR (balanced plug, cage-guided) control valve. Trim options described include standard beveled/radiused-seat trims (trims 1, 4, 27, 28, 29, 37/37H, 57, 85-87 for NACE/sour service), the Whisper Trim I/III and Whisper NXG cages and WhisperFlo cages, the Cavitrol III one- and two-stage cavitation-control cages, TSO (tight shutoff) trim, restricted-capacity trim, and the optional Trim Cartridge (with ENVIRO-SEAL PTFE, graphite ULF or duplex packing). The trims for high pressure drop and noise service are the low-noise Whisper Trim/Whisper NXG/WhisperFlo cages (aerodynamic noise attenuation) and the Cavitrol III cages (cavitation/pressure-drop control); e.g. Whisper Trim III/NXG allow up to 0.999*AP/P1 and trims 4/29 up to 99 bar (1440 psi) with clean dry gas, while standard trims are limited to lower drops (e.g. 21 bar for other fluids).

final.answer: The valve operated by control loop FIC-12-1 is FV-12-1, a Fisher ET / EAT / ETR globe control valve. It comes in sizes NPS 1, 1-1/2, 2, 2-1/2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 (DN 25, 40, 50, 65, 80, 100, 150 or 200), with the exact available sizes depending on the product variant and end connection — for example, flanged ET bodies span the full range, while socket-weld ET bodies come only in NPS 1, 1-1/2 or 2. Since NPS 3 (DN 80) is among the available sizes, your 3-inch line can be accommodated. Note that the datasheet does not state a specific line size for this installation; line size and schedule must be specified when ordering.

trace.content: Regarding GV-10-1 on the P&ID: Can it be switched on continuously all shift, or will the coil overheat?

{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "GV-10-1", "question": "What is the duty cycle / continuous operation rating of the solenoid coil? Can it be energized continuously without overheating (e.g., 100% ED rating)?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet gfps-165-solenoid-valve, pages [2, 5, 1, 4]:
Yes — the datasheet rates the coil for continuous operation: "Nominal mode of operation = Continuous operation 100 % ED" [p. 2]. "ED" stands for duty ratio (relative energized time), so 100 % ED means the solenoid can stay energized continuously without overheating.

Additional relevant facts from the same Specifications table on page 2:

- Insulation class of the coil: Class H (a higher heat-resistant insulation class)
- Mode of operation: "A" (listed for each nominal diameter DN 15 to DN 50)
- Power consumption in operation: 11 VA for AC versions and 5 W for DC versions, depending on current type and nominal diameter (see the Kv 100 values table on page 2)
- Supply voltage: 24 V DC, 230 V 50 Hz/60 Hz, 115 V 50 Hz/60 Hz, with a voltage tolerance of ±10 %

The datasheet does not give a maximum continuous energization time limit beyond the 100 % ED rating.

The factory default is High alarm (≥ 21.75 mA; ≥ 22.5 mA for some option codes), with Low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA (≤ 3.6 mA for NAMUR NE 43 option codes C4/CN, and custom levels 20.2–23.0 mA high / 3.6–3.8 mA low with option code C1). To change the direction, set the alarm level configuration (jumper/switch selection) on the transmitter; the datasheet does not give step-by-step procedures beyond noting the selection is made via the jumper/switch.

{"answer": "FT-10-1", "not_present": false}
{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "FT-10-1", "question": "On failure of the transmitter, does the output signal fail high or low, and what is the configurable alarm/fail direction setting?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [88, 26, 15, 74, 63, 52, 42, 85]:
**It can be either — high or low failure mode is user-selectable with a jumper/switch on the transmitter.** When the self-diagnostics detect a sensor or microprocessor failure, the analog signal is driven either high or low to alert the user (for the HART 4–20 mA output, option code A) [p. 88].

The actual alarm current depends on the alarm level configuration (see Table 5 on page 88):

- **Default:** High alarm ≥ 21.75 mA; Low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA. Note: for some options (codes M6, DA1, T9, RK), the high alarm default is ≥ 22.5 mA.
- **NAMUR compliant** (NAMUR NE 43 analog levels; option codes C4 or CN): High alarm ≥ 22.5 mA; Low alarm ≤ 3.6 mA.
- **Custom levels** (requires option code C1): High alarm 20.2–23.0 mA; Low alarm 3.6–3.8 mA. Note: the low alarm must be 0.1 mA less than low saturation and the high alarm 0.1 mA greater than high saturation.

For other outputs: with the 1–5 Vdc low-power output (code M), on a gross failure the signal is driven either below 0.94 V (low) or above 5.4 V (high), selectable by internal jumper [p. 88]. With outputs F, W, and X (Fieldbus/Profibus/wireless), failure information is passed as an alert and a status along with the process variable, not as a high/low signal level [p. 88].

The datasheet also notes the alarm levels ordering option is only available with the HART 4–20 mA output (code A), and the standard factory configuration ships with the alarm set to High (not applicable to FOUNDATION Fieldbus, PROFIBUS PA, or wireless) [p. 26, 42, 74, 109, 110].

score.reason: Jumper selection, default high and standard/NAMUR/custom levels given; output M jumper missing.

Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [66, 108, 74, 10, 20, 42, 110, 100]:
Yes — the flange's process connection can be 1/4 NPT, and yes, a manifold is offered as an option (factory-assembled integral manifolds).

**Process connection**
- For the Rosemount 3051C, the process connections are 1/4-18 NPT on 2 1/8-inch centers and 1/2-14 NPT on 2-, 2 1/8- or 2 1/4-inch centers [p. 91].
- Ordering data lists "connection = 1/4-inch NPT" together with flange classes such as DIN 2501 PN 25/40 with pipe size DN 100, DIN 2501 PN 10/16 with DN 100, and ASME B16.5 (ANSI) 300 with pipe size 4 (102) — so the 1/4-inch NPT connection applies depending on the selected flange class and pipe size (no page given for these rows).
- For other models the connection differs: e.g. the Rosemount 3051CFP can have "pipe ends: NPT threaded" (option code P1, p. 55), and the Rosemount 3051T has its own process connection style table (1/2-14 NPT female, G1/2 male, coned and threaded, or non-threaded instrument flange, p. 20).

**Manifold**
- Yes. For the Rosemount 3051C there is a "Manifold assembly" ordering option (p. 10): code S5 = assemble to Rosemount 305 Integral Manifold, and code S6 = assemble to Rosemount 304 Manifold or Connection System (both starred offerings). Note the requirement on that page: "assemble-to" items are specified separately and require a completed model number — i.e. the manifold is ordered as a separate line item that is assembled to the transmitter, not part of the base transmitter.
- The datasheet also states that optional Rosemount 304, 305 or 306 integral manifolds ("integral manifold" = a manifold built directly onto the transmitter) can be factory assembled to Rosemount 3051C and 3051T transmitters [p. 110].
- For the remote-mount versions (3051CFA and 3051CFC), separate ordering tables list "Manifold for remote mount option" codes, e.g. F2 = 3-valve manifold SST, F3 = 3-valve manifold alloy C-276, F6 = 5-valve manifold SST, F7 = 5-valve manifold alloy C-276 (3051CFA, p. 42; 3051CFC, p. 51).

I could not find in the facts a single statement naming the process connection for the flanged (3051L-type) models specifically as 1/4 NPT — for those, the high-side process connection sizes listed are 2 in / DN 50, 3 in / DN 80 and 4 in / DN 100 (p. 66).

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 3, 14, 18, 6, 23, 26, 13]:
**Direct answer:** The datasheet lists several cage/trim options for the ET, EAT and ETR valves, and the ones intended for noise (and, via their pressure-drop capability, high pressure drop) are the Whisper trims: Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim and WhisperFlo cages.

**Trim options found in the datasheet:**
- Standard cages (quick-opening, linear or equal percentage flow) [p. 2, 4]
- Whisper Trim III cages [p. 4, 16]
- Whisper NXG Trim cages [p. 4, 13]
- WhisperFlo cages [p. 4]
- Cavitrol III cages (one-stage and two-stage) [p. 4, 16, 6]
- TSO (Tight Shutoff) trim [p. 6]
- Restricted-capacity and full-sized trims [p. 2]
- Trim Cartridge (a factory-assembled replaceable trim unit, available for some ET configurations) [p. 6]

**Which one is for noise / high pressure drop:**
- The Whisper Trim and WhisperFlo cages provide "aerodynamic noise attenuation" [p. 2], and Whisper Trim III and Whisper NXG Trim cages are limited to a maximum pressure drop of 0.999 ΔP/P1 (a ratio close to the full inlet pressure, meaning they can take very large pressure drops) [p. 3]. Figure 8 on page 16 shows a "Metal Seat and Whisper Trim III Cage in Fisher ET Valve", and Figure 6 on page 9 shows a "Typical Valve with WhisperFlo Aerodynamic or Whisper NXG Trim".
- The Cavitrol III cages, by contrast, are for cavitation protection (not noise) [p. 2]; Figure 10 on page 16 shows the Cavitrol III One-Stage Cage.
- The regular trims (Trims 1, 4, 27, 29, 37, 37H, 85, 87, etc.) are the standard trims for valves without these special cages — see Figures 13, 14 and 15 on pages 18, 19 and 26, which give their maximum pressure drops and temperature limits per body/seat material and fluid conditions.

So: if the problem is high noise or a very high pressure drop, the Whisper options (Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim, WhisperFlo) are the intended choice; Cavitrol III is the choice for cavitation. The datasheet does not, in the facts I have, give a single "high pressure drop" trim number recommendation beyond what is described above.

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 5, 3, 2, 21, 23, 22, 24]:
Yes, the Fisher ET is the valve itself — specifically the valve body (and its complete valve assembly, including trim), not a separate component.

According to the datasheet, the Fisher ET is a **single-port, globe-style control valve with cage guiding, a balanced valve plug, and push-down-to-close valve plug action** [p. 3]. It is part of the Fisher "easy-e" valve family [p. 2], and is used for **throttling or on-off control of a wide variety of liquids and gases** [p. 2].

Details to note:

- **The valve family / related variants**: The bulletin actually covers three variants:
  - **ET** – single-port, globe-style control valve, push-down-to-close [p. 3]
  - **EAT** – an angle version of the ET control valve, used to facilitate piping or where a self-draining valve is desired [p. 3]
  - **ETR** – same as ET but with push-down-to-open valve plug action [p. 3]

- **Valve sizes**: available from NPS 1 up to NPS 8 (NPS = nominal pipe size in inches). Weights range from about 14 kg (30 lb) for NPS 1 to about 408 kg (900 lb) for NPS 8 [p. 4].

- **Body materials** (body, bonnet and bonnet spacer or bottom flange): cast iron, WCC or LCC carbon steel, WC9 chrome moly steel, CF8M (cast 316 stainless steel), CF3M (cast 316L stainless steel), or other materials upon request [p. 3].

- **Guiding / plug type**: all three designs use cage guiding, single ports, and balanced valve plugs [p. 2].

- **Seating**: metal-to-PTFE seating is standard in all valves except those with Cavitrol III cages (where metal-to-metal seating is standard, for higher temperatures); metal-to-metal seating is optional for all other valves [p. 2].

So in short: "Fisher ET" names the whole globe-style control valve (which is centered on its valve body), while EAT is the angle-body version and ETR the push-down-to-open version of the same design [pp. 2–3].

score.reason: Single-port globe-style control valve, cage-guided, balanced plug.

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 6, 3, 13, 12, 27, 18, 29]:
I could not find in these facts anything specifically identifying the tag "FV-11-1" — the datasheet describes the Fisher ET valve family in general, not that specific tag number. Here is what the datasheet does say, which should apply if FV-11-1 is an Fisher ET:

**Valve type:** The ET is a single-port, globe-style control valve with cage guiding, a balanced valve plug, and push-down-to-close valve plug action (see Figure 3) [p. 3]. Valve plug type is balanced valve plugs for all three designs (ET, EAT, ETR) [p. 2].

**Seating / seat options:** Depending on the construction chosen, the valve has either PTFE seating (a soft plastic seat) or metal seating; constructions with Cavitrol III cages always use metal seating [p. 6]. The ET is also available with soft seat [p. 7] and with TSO ("Tight Shutoff") trim, which has a replaceable, protected soft seat [p. 6]. Seat, plug and cage materials depend on the trim number — see the tables: Table 8 for standard trims, Table 9 for Cavitrol III, Table 11 for WhisperFlo, Table 12 for Whisper Trim III / NXG, and Table 23 for sour-service (NACE) trims (e.g. Trim 1: seat ring S41600 HT or CA15 HT; Trim 4: disk seat/retainer S31600 for PTFE seat) [p. 10, 13, 27].

**Leakage class (shutoff):** Shutoff classes are per ANSI/FCI 70-2 and IEC 60534-4 — Class IV, V or VI; see Tables 4, 6 or 7 [p. 3]. Details from Table 4 [p. 6]:
- Class IV is standard for metal seating (all except Cavitrol III cages, and Cavitrol III one-stage cage).
- Class V is optional for metal or PTFE seating; for metal seating it requires a spring-loaded seal ring, radius-seat plug and wide-bevel seat ring (not available with 8-in. port, quick-opening cage; not with trims 4, 29 and 85).
- Class VI is optional (see Table 6); both soft seat and metal seat ET constructions can provide Class VI shut-off [p. 7].
- Cavitrol III two-stage cage construction: Class V (metal seating).
- TSO trim: not an ANSI/FCI leakage class — valves with TSO trim are factory tested to a more stringent Emerson requirement of no leakage at time of shipment; test medium is water; specify service P when ordering; shutoff class V.
- Class V shutoff for ET is available up to 232 °C / 450 °F using PEEK anti-extrusion rings [p. 4].
- Also, the Trim Cartridge option comes factory seat-leak tested to Class V shutoff [p. 6].

**Inspection/testing instructions:** The datasheet facts mention the factory testing noted above (TSO water test, Trim Cartridge Class V seat-leak test), but I could not find any general inspection or testing instructions for the valve in the facts provided.

**Trim capabilities / pressure drops:** See Figure 13 on page 18, which shows pressure drop versus fluid temperature for the trims with PTFE seating and with optional metal seating for various body materials [p. 18]; Figure 14 on page 19 shows the typical trim for Cavitrol III cage constructions; Figures 13, 14 and 15 are also referenced for maximum pressure drops, and the maximum pressure drop must not exceed the lowest value of the chosen material combination [p. 3, 32].

Note: when ordering, the datasheet asks you to specify the shutoff classification required, plus pressure drops (minimum, normal, maximum flowing, and maximum at shutoff) [p. 32].
